review_scope: Targeted primary-source and code-unit comparison; not an exhaustive Scopus/Google Scholar review.

sources.title: Convex and Non-Convex Approaches for Statistical Inference with Class-Conditional Noisy Labels
sources.prior_overlap: Corrected convex logistic surrogate with an affine pseudo-response outside the binary probability range; high-dimensional penalized estimation and testing.
sources.scope_difference: Their stated high-dimensional convex estimator includes an l1 penalty. The present row-weight comparison concerns unrestricted compensated attainment, its explicit scale profile, and fixed-dimensional covariance at different weights. An objective or assumption difference alone is not evidence of priority.
sources.PDF_screenshot_access: Cache-miss errors; publisher PDF text and displayed formula extraction were readable.

sources.title: Sharp Guarantees and Optimal Performance for Inference in Binary and Gaussian-Mixture Models
sources.prior_overlap: Sharp high-dimensional binary convex-loss analysis, optimal-loss comparisons and ordinary separation thresholds.
sources.scope_difference: These inspected units already cover generic existence/performance distinctions and ordinary separation. They do not directly supply the subtracted two-sample loss calculation. No claim of a new CGMT or generic risk/existence trade-off is made.

sources.title: Prediction-Powered Inference with Inverse Probability Weighting
sources.prior_overlap: Weighted prediction correction and HT/Hajek normalization for informative labeling.
sources.scope_difference: The present law has independent IID samples and a known utility multiplier; all three loss terms use a fixed weight and original sample counts. Its claim concerns the compensated support event and explicit variance cost, not introduction of weighted PPI or survey correction.

GitHub_learning.inspected_unit: ppi_estimators: weighted rectifier and its variance calculation
GitHub_learning.lesson: Read the exact weight normalization and target before comparing a weighted procedure. The published example is mean inference under informative labeling, not the current logistic target.

primary_queries: unbiased logistic loss unbounded below noisy
claimed_increment: Within the same known-scale compensated objective: the row weight maximizing its existence boundary differs from the one minimizing full regular oracle covariance; a fixed power-weight path has first-order capacity improvement and second-order initial covariance cost.
not_claimed: new generic Gaussian or support geometry
optimal high-dimensional risk or intermediate-weight Pareto frontier
